<badge color="success">Best overall for RVs</badge>

<title size="xl">BLUETTI AC200L — $899</title>

<row align=start gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view RV power station" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="132px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity value="BLUETTI AC200L" category="product" disambig="2048Wh portable LiFePO4 power station"/>**

    <title color="success" size="2xl" tabularNums={true}>$899</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Listed price, October 2026</text>
    - 2,048Wh LiFePO4 battery
    - 2,400W continuous AC output
    - Built-in TT-30 RV outlet
    - 1,200W maximum solar input
    - Discount code: `AFF5OFF` saves $44.95
  </box>
</row>

**Why I recommend it**

The biggest advantage is its built-in TT-30 RV outlet. You can connect your RV's shore-power cord directly, without needing an additional adapter setup.

It can handle typical RV essentials:
- Refrigerator
- Water pump
- Interior lights
- Coffee maker
- Laptops and other electronics

One important limitation: its RV outlet delivers approximately 20A, not the full 30A RV service. It is not designed to run a typical rooftop RV air conditioner.

Also, switch a two-way RV refrigerator to propane rather than leaving it on automatic mode. An electric fridge can consume 2.4–3.6kWh daily, exceeding the entire battery capacity. <Cite refs={["turn356295view0"]}/>

## Other strong contenders

<box gap={3}>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="104px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **<Entity value="Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2" category="product"/>**
      <title size="lg" tabularNums={true}>$899.99</title>
      - 2kWh-class capacity
      - Built-in TT-30 RV outlet
      - Lightest option at 41.7 lb
      - Best if portability is a priority
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Renogy PowerStation 2000 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="104px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **<Entity value="Renogy PowerStation 2000" category="product"/>**
      <title size="lg" tabularNums={true}>$849</title>
      - 2,048Wh capacity
      - 2,400W output
      - 3,600W surge
      - Attractive lower-price alternative
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="104px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **<Entity value="BLUETTI Elite 200 V2" category="product"/>**
      <title size="lg" tabularNums={true}>$899</title>
      - 2,074Wh capacity
      - 2,600W output
      - 53.4 lb
      - Excellent battery longevity: 6,000-cycle rating
      - Best value if a built-in TT-30 outlet isn't essential
    </box>
  </row>
</box>
<Cite refs={["turn356295view0"]}/>

## My final recommendation

| Your priority | Best choice |
|---|---|
| Best overall RV integration | BLUETTI AC200L |
| Lightest RV-friendly option | Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 |
| Lower purchase price | Renogy PowerStation 2000 |
| Long battery lifespan | BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 |

**My pick: BLUETTI AC200L.** For an RV owner spending less than $900, the combination of 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, and a built-in TT-30 outlet makes it particularly compelling.

One caveat: the AC200L is an older model, and its availability should be confirmed before purchasing. The supplied results reported it in stock on BLUETTI's US website on October 31, 2026. <Cite refs={["turn356295view0"]}/>

You can read the detailed comparison here: [Dealectric – Best 2kWh Power Station for RV Under $900](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv).
